title: Prototype: elastic cell-measurement layer and column reflow model
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Our existing virtualized table presents janky column-resize interactions and inconsistent cell wrapping when users change density or rapidly resize columns. Performance engineers have identified repeated DOM measurements during continuous resize as a major CPU hotspot for large tables (10k+ rows). Designers have also observed confusing visual jumps when fractional pixel rounding and nested content (avatars, chips, badges) are involved.

Objective: Prototype an "elastic cell-measurement" layer that decouples measurement from paint hot paths and a column reflow model that supports fractional widths, transient elasticity during drag, and graceful rounding reconciliation after drag ends. The goal is to make resize feel smooth at 60fps for typical mid-range devices while preserving accurate hit targets and accessible keyboard/assistive interactions.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce a measurement cache keyed by visible range + column id + density token set. Measurements are taken off the main drag loop and are updated incrementally using a prioritised queue.
- During drag, apply a lightweight "elastic transform" to the column header and visible cells (CSS transform translateX + scaleX) instead of adjusting layout immediately, which avoids reflow of offscreen rows.
- After drag completes, reconcile the transform with the layout by committing the final widths; run a batched layout update that uses cached measurements to avoid repeated getBoundingClientRect calls.
- Support fractional widths internally (store widths as float) and only snap to device pixels at commit time with an algorithm that distributes rounding drift across adjacent columns to avoid visible jumps.
- Density integration: precompute measurement deltas for our token-dense/compact/comfort modes and incorporate those into the cache so switching density is near-instant for visible ranges.
- Accessibility: keyboard resize uses discrete steps informed by token grid; announce interim values via live region and provide aria-valuenow for assistive tech. Focus outline must remain stable during elastic transforms.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Complexity: measurement cache adds state and invalidation rules. We need clear heuristics for when to invalidate (column visibility change, font-size/dpi change, dynamic content mutation).
- Edge cases: cells that lazy-load images or render asynchronously may cause measurement drift; fallback is to flag stale measurement and force one synchronous measurement at commit.
- Browser variability: transforms for elastic feel may differ in behavior on low-end GPUs; provide a fallback path that does immediate layout if transform budget exceeded.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- High-fidelity Figma prototype demonstrating elastic header drag and density switch animation (micro-interaction specs).
- A design spec summarising measurement cache rules, UX states (idle, dragging, reconciling), keyboard flows, and accessible announcement strings.
- Implementation notes for ENG: example measurement cache key shapes, suggested debounce/throttle values, recommended CSS transforms and will-change hints.

Success metrics:
- Perceived smoothness: 90th percentile frames during resize improved from 40fps to >=50fps on our mid-tier benchmark device.
- Reduced sync layout calls during drag by >=70% for tables with >5 columns and >2k rows.
- No regressions in keyboard accessibility tests and correct announcements in NVDA/VoiceOver smoke tests.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with interactive header drag and density toggle provided and reviewed by Design
Design spec published in Confluence with measurement cache invariants and keyboard/aria copy
Engineering spike PR demonstrating elastic transform approach merged to feature branch with perf telemetry
Automated tests covering key invalidation cases and keyboard resize behaviour
No accessibility failures in manual NVDA/VoiceOver smoke tests on supported browsers
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Kapoor: Kickoff design spike. Ran quick experiments with transform-only drag in a sandbox. Initial feel is promising but images in cells break measurement assumptions.

2026-02-24 - Marco Hernandez: Implemented a PoC that toggles between transform and layout commit. Observed 65% fewer layout thrashes in the synthetic benchmark. Pushed PoC branch and linked PR in attachments.

2026-02-26 - Sophie Liao (PM): Noted that customer-facing product teams want the density switch to be instant even when many rows are visible; please include a fallback that uses the cache to recompute visible range only.

2026-03-01 - Accessibility review (Jamal Peterson): Keyboard behaviour looks good; request to ensure aria-live announcements don't spam when user holds arrow keys — propose 300ms throttle on live region updates.

2026-03-05 - Marco Hernandez: Updated implementation notes to include rounding distribution algorithm for fractional widths. Ran tests on Win11/Chrome and macOS/Safari — animation parity looks acceptable.

2026-03-10 - Design review (Aisha Kapoor): Reviewed Figma prototype with motion and microinteraction details. Minor tweak: increase drag elasticity damping from 0.18 to 0.25 to reduce overshoot on mobile browsers.

2026-03-12 - Marco Hernandez: Merged spike branch into feature/elastic-measurement for cross-team integration testing. Marking ticket evolving toward In Review for design sign-off once ENG stability checks complete.
